picks.style: ancient greek chorus, seven-stringed lyre and libyan pipe, aged male voices in unison, celebratory, moderate, swelling
picks.why: The old singers' ode to song itself — Graces and Muses linked forever, the swan-voiced poet who will not stop praising.

picks.style: ancient greek lament, kithara and low aulos, grieving female voice answered by a broken male voice, slow, desolate
picks.why: Megara asking which child to kiss first, wishing she could gather her sighs like a bee; fortune taking a life like a feather.

picks.style: ancient greek tragic chorus, frantic frame drums and shrill aulos, layered voices, accelerating, terrifying
picks.why: Madness driving her chariot with a hundred hissing serpent-heads — 'the dance begins without the cymbals' crash'.

picks.style: greek pastoral epigram, lyre and soft reed pipe, single warm voice, unhurried, open-air
picks.why: Nicaenetus preferring the country to the city feast — a willow-branch bed and the zephyr freshening the heart.

picks.style: greek symposium song, aulos and hand drum, sardonic male voice with chorus, steady, argumentative
picks.why: The attack on athletes — will they fight the enemy with a quoit in hand? — a whole verse argument with a punchline.

picks.style: comic patter song, plucked lyre and light percussion, sly tenor, brisk, short-breathed lines
picks.why: The parasite's self-portrait in short skipping lines: two well-made garments, a rich fool in the forum, and laughter on demand.

picks.style: american pastoral ballad, acoustic guitar and low strings, clear female vocal, elegiac, unhurried
picks.why: Colma's dying speech — a spring eternal and a nightless sky far to the west, where souls keep their old feelings.

picks.style: colonial fireside song, fiddle and dulcimer, mellow tenor, lilting, moderate
picks.why: 'O gentle sleep, wrap me in dreams, of fields and woods, and running streams' — then the darker draught of Lethe.

picks.style: roman stage cantica, tibia and soft strings, low tenor, grave, tender, slow
picks.why: Chrysis on her deathbed handing over the girl — 'husband, friend, protector, father' — clean monologue, no stage business.

picks.style: georgian love song, harpsichord and strings, light tenor, dancing, amorous, moderate
picks.why: The Martial imitation's counting refrain — bees on Hybla, flowers, flocks, sands, stars — and still craving more kisses.

picks.style: mock-elegy, baroque chamber strings and recorder, plaintive countertenor, ceremonious, slow
picks.why: The funeral of Matzel the bullfinch — linnets and doves summoned to beat their wings and drop the natural tear.

picks.style: welsh tavern ballad, fiddle and pipe, hearty baritone with chorus, jaunty, fast
picks.why: The Harriet Hanbury ballad, with its 'Sir' tag ending every stanza and the ale going dead while the Welshmen gaze.

picks.style: dionysian hymn, aulos, frame drum and finger cymbals, layered voices, intoxicating, building
picks.why: Wine running through the black ship, the vine spreading along the sail, ivy on the mast, garlands on the thole-pins.

picks.style: homeric hymn, kithara over drone, single male voice, narrative, measured, mysterious
picks.why: The god on the headland with waving dark hair, the bonds falling from his hands while he sits smiling.

picks.style: greek epiphany hymn, roaring low drums and shrill pipes, big male chorus, savage then radiant
picks.why: The lion and the shaggy bear on deck, the sailors leaping overboard into dolphins, and the helmsman spared.

picks.style: oracular chant, aulos drone and struck bronze, grave female voice, hushed, slow, foreboding
picks.why: Only candidate, and it is the Apollo oracle itself — 'a tomb shall be the bridal chamber for both, and destroying fire'.

picks.style: latin hexameter setting, lyre and low flutes, sonorous male voice, stately, slow, chamber
picks.why: Only candidate; the Virgil and Horace lines still sing in Latin — the wished-for boar, the bird fearing the snake over her fledglings.
